configuration.source: replay of matched_budget_emergence.run_seed with identical seeds

coverage_definition.good_post: viable_post restricted to candidates with changed-goal utility >= tau
coverage_definition.niche: sim.niche(candidate, bins): adaptability x efficiency cells
coverage_definition.scope: what the arm's search produced after the change, identically defined for all five arms; not what each arm retains
coverage_definition.viable_post: cells holding a panel-accepted, truly viable candidate proposed after the change

evidence_level: synthetic mechanism; no real agents or humans

improvement_definition.cost: proposals per improvement; one proposal is one verification attempt in this benchmark, so the two are equal by contract
improvement_definition.improvement: an accepted candidate whose changed-goal utility exceeds the running best by more than the materiality; the running best starts at the best changed-goal utility among everything the arm had verified before the change

modes.carry: running best starts at the best changed-goal utility among everything the arm verified before the change
modes.fresh: running best starts at zero when the goal changes, so an arm is credited for re-finding what it already held

improvement_definition.pooled_ratio: ratio of summed proposals to summed improvements, because a single seed can have zero improvements

limitations: All candidates, goals, verdicts and costs are synthetic; this is mechanism evidence, not evidence about real agents or people.
The threshold is a fraction of a reference optimum of this landscape; the fraction is a choice, which is why a five-point grid is reported next to it.
Coverage counts niches the search produced, not niches an arm retains. A random-search arm scatters proposals and is advantaged on produced coverage by construction.

An improvement count rewards incremental climbing (many small records) unless materiality is raised, and depends on whether earlier verified work carries over, so it is reported at two materialities and under both carry-over modes.
Proposal counts are a compute proxy only; the E024 matched budget makes them equal per arm, so only the improvement count differs.
The E024 perfect panel is used, so no false accept can inflate an arm's coverage or improvements.

multiple_comparisons.note: p-values are exact and uncorrected; read them against this alpha, and read the threshold and materiality grids as part of the same family

not_measured: human attention: nothing here models a person reading, deciding or waiting, and proposal counts are not a proxy for it
novelty and information gain: no novelty score or information measure is defined on candidates in this landscape, and none is invented here
churn: agents never join or leave in the E024 arms
energy and wall time: a proposal is a unit, not a joule or a second
post-integration defects and adversarial contributors: outside the E024 perfect-panel arms (E027 and E036 model them separately)

threshold_rule.censoring: a seed that never reaches tau within the horizon is right-censored: its time is at least the horizon, it counts as not reached, and it contributes the horizon (a lower bound) to restricted means
threshold_rule.fixed_before: the primary fraction was fixed before any aggregate was computed; seed 0's traces were viewed once while checking the replay

optimum.method: grid over reliability x security at step 0.005, greedy fill of the remaining budget by goal weight

readings.first_passage: first post-change generation with delivered utility >= tau
readings.sustained: first generation from which delivered utility stays >= tau through the last generation

threshold_rule.rule: tau = fraction * optimum, where optimum is the best utility any viable candidate can reach under the changed goal
threshold_rule.why_absolute: E024's recovery_generations compares an arm with 95% of its own final value, so an arm that stays on a low plateau recovers at generation 0. A threshold on the utility scale itself, derived from the landscape and not from any arm, cannot be passed by standing still.
